list.empty: No sessions yet. Add one to keep an address, a user and the credentials for it together.
list.removeMessage: Delete “{name}”? The stored password or key reference goes with it.
list.importMissingKeys: {count} session names a key this device does not hold | {count} sessions name a key this device does not hold
list.importDroppedHops: {count} session lost a jump host the file did not carry | {count} sessions lost a jump host the file did not carry
list.exportMessage: Write every saved session and group to one file. Anyone who can read that file can read the addresses, user names and jump hosts in it.
list.exportIncludeSecretsHint: They are written in plain text. Leave this off unless the file is going somewhere you trust.
list.exportDone: {count} session written to {file} | {count} sessions written to {file}
list.dropOutOfGroups: Move it out of every group
list.failureHint: Could not connect. Click for the reason.
list.removeSelectedMessage: Delete the session you picked? Its stored password or key reference goes with it. | Delete the {count} sessions you picked? Their stored passwords or key references go with them.
list.regexHint: Match session names, addresses and users with JavaScript regular expressions.
list.groupRemoveMessage: Delete the group “{name}”? Its sessions move out of every group and its subgroups move to the top level — nothing inside a group is deleted with it.

editor.description: Where the machine is, who to log in as, and how this build authenticates.
editor.name: Name
editor.methodUnsupported: This build does not implement Pageant yet, so it is not selectable.

secret.label: Password
secret.storedPlaceholder: Saved password — leave empty to keep it
secret.stored: A password is already stored. It is kept unless a new one is typed here.
secret.notStored: No password is stored for this session yet, so it cannot connect until one is saved.

key.hasPassphrase: The key file has a passphrase
key.passphraseHint: The passphrase is read together with the key and stored with it; it is asked for before the file is opened.
key.name: File
key.passphraseStored: A passphrase is stored with this key.
key.noPassphraseStored: No passphrase is stored with this key.
key.forgetMessage: Forget “{name}”? The key is deleted from the vault, and a session that used it will ask for it again.

jumps.title: Jump hosts
jumps.note: Connected in this order, before this session: the first directly, and each next one through the one before it. Every hop's key is verified before anything is sent through it.
jumps.empty: None. This session is reached directly.
jumps.missingTip: This hop names a saved session that has since been deleted. It is kept here so it is removed on purpose.

forwards.title: Port forwards
forwards.hint: The left side is a port on this machine; the right side is where it leads on the far side. A bind port of 0 asks the system for a free one.
forwards.empty: None. This session opens no local ports.

validation.bindHost: Enter the address to listen on.
validation.bindPort: The bind port must be a number between 0 and 65535; 0 asks the system for a free one.
validation.targetHost: Enter the host the forward leads to.
validation.targetPort: The target port must be a number between 1 and 65535.

validation.name: Give this session a name.
validation.host: Enter the host name or address.
validation.user: Enter the user to log in as.
validation.port: The port must be a number between 1 and 65535.
validation.key: Attach a key file for public-key authentication.

terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.forwardAgent: Let this server use the key agent on this machine
terminal.forwardAgentNote: While the session is open, anything running on that server can ask for signatures. Leave it off unless the server needs it.
terminal.recordNote: A recording is a plain file on disk holding everything the terminal shows, in a format players like asciinema read. It goes in the recordings folder beside the settings.

hostKey.unknownTitle: A host key that has not been seen before
hostKey.unknownBody: Nothing has been sent to this server yet — no user name, no password, no key. Trusting the key records it and connects; if it is not the key you expect, cancel.
hostKey.mismatchTitle: The server is presenting a different host key
hostKey.mismatchBody: The key recorded for this address is not the one being presented now. Someone may be intercepting the connection, or the machine may have been rebuilt. Nothing was sent to that server.
hostKey.replace: Forget the old key and trust this one
hostKey.replaceWarning: This removes the key you trusted before. It cannot be undone, and it is the choice an attacker would like you to make.
